quotes.text: The tool doesn't replace your judgment, it sharpens it. You still decide what counts as valid input and how error should guide the user
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Balanced take on AI-assisted coding: Copilot supports but does not replace developer judgment.

quotes.text: A message like invalid input is the software equivalent of a locked door with no sign. It tells users nothing, so they guess, fail again, and eventually throw the problem at you.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Vivid explanation of why vague validation messages create support tickets.

quotes.text: You iterate it into armor, and the workflow is simple enough to remember, like a four step loop. Generate the skeleton, ask Copilot to improve error messages, then add edge case handling, and finally deploy.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Concrete, repeatable workflow for hardening generated validation code.

quotes.text: Copilot makes strong suggestions, but it's not a guarantee. Always review and test before deploying to production. Treat their outputs as a strategy guide, not as instant loot.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Clear recommendation to review and test AI-generated code before production.

takeaways: Prefixing prompts with @powerpages in GitHub Copilot Chat gives context-aware code for Liquid templates, Dataverse bindings and form validation instead of generic web snippets.
Validation scripts get production-ready by iterating in the same chat: generate a skeleton, improve error messages, handle edge cases, then deploy.
Downloading site content with the Power Platform CLI into VS Code keeps editing, Copilot assistance and deployment in one workspace, though some features are preview and controlled by tenant admins.
hook: Power Pages form validation breaking and Liquid errors eating your evenings? This episode is for Power Pages makers and developers working in VS Code. Learn how the @powerpages participant in GitHub Copilot Chat writes, explains and hardens your code in context.
